question: With no new GPU budget yet, invest next in more supervised examples or another small GRPO run?

queries.query: supervised fine tuning versus reinforcement learning verifiable rewards reasoning small data Qwen
supervised fine tuning versus reinforcement learning verifiable rewards reasoning small data Qwen
supervised fine tuning versus reinforcement learning verifiable rewards reasoning small data Qwen

sources.title: Supervised Reinforcement Learning: From Expert Trajectories to Step-wise Reasoning
Med-RLVR: Emerging Medical Reasoning from a 3B base model via reinforcement Learning

recommendation: Invest the next annotation effort in targeted, manually corrected supervised examples, while deferring all training until supported-answer labels and a held-out comparison exist. Do not schedule another GRPO run now.

claims.text: The SRL authors caution that SFT on modest sets of long demonstrations may overfit and report that both SFT and outcome-based RL struggle on challenging tasks.
Med-RLVR uses an outcome correctness and format verifier for its medical multiple-choice reward.

baseline: The existing 35 replay-verified trajectories and v5 SFT checkpoint; retain the current no-training policy.
matched_test: Without GPU, independently review the 20 answerable development cases, categorize unsupported answers and execution faults, and draft/replay corrections for distinct answer-support failures. Before any later training, hold out named questions and compare an equal-compute corrected-example SFT run with a GRPO run only if a semantic reward can be validated.
decision_rule: Training threshold explicitly unset until named held-out tasks and independent human support judgments exist. Proceed to GRPO only after its reward agrees with human support judgments on a prespecified validation set; agreement threshold currently unset.
uncertainty: The cited studies concern math, software tasks, and medical multiple choice, not this paper reader. The 3/20 provisional answer result has not been independently reviewed. SFT can overfit small demonstrations.

question: For long papers, keep BM25 passage search or test hybrid retrieval plus reranking?

sources.title: SciRet: A Compute-Aware Empirical Study of Retrieval and Reranking for Scientific RAG
Lit3R: Retrieve-Relate-Read for Evidence-Grounded Question Answering over Scientific Literature

recommendation: Keep BM25 as the production baseline and test BM25 plus dense rank fusion. Treat reranking as a separate ablation, not part of the default candidate.

claims.text: SciRet reports hybrid BM25 plus dense recall gains in its scientific corpus, while an MS MARCO cross-encoder reduced precision in its tested setup.
Lit3R combines sparse and dense retrieval with reranking for literature-grounded QA.

baseline: Current BM25 passage search with the same segmentation and passage budget.
matched_test: On identical long-paper questions and cached passages, compare BM25, BM25+dense fusion, then fusion+reranker. Blindly assess whether answer-support spans enter the top-k and whether the fixed reader gives supported answers; measure local indexing, retrieval, and end-to-end latency.
decision_rule: Promote hybrid only if it recovers at least 3 more support spans among 40 questions and loses no more than 1 span found by BM25, with no decrease in independently reviewed supported answers. Reranker must improve at least 2 additional support-span hits beyond hybrid; latency ceiling unset pending hardware measurement.
uncertainty: SciRet uses CORD-19 with pseudo-relevance labels, so its retrieval scores are not a QASPER prediction. A generic cross-encoder may reduce precision in this domain; paper-specific retrieval and reranking costs are unknown.

question: For two concurrent Qwen3-8B readers, focus next latency test on prefix caching or speculative decoding?

queries.query: prefix caching versus speculative decoding concurrent LLM serving latency shared prompts
prefix caching versus speculative decoding concurrent LLM serving latency shared prompts

sources.title: KVFlow: Efficient Prefix Caching for Accelerating LLM-Based Multi-Agent Workflows
Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding

recommendation: Measure prefix reuse and prefix caching first for two concurrent readers; defer speculative decoding until output decode time is shown to dominate.

claims.text: KVFlow reports that its prefix-cache gains shrink as outputs grow because decoding dominates runtime.
Speculative decoding targets serial autoregressive decode steps by drafting and verifying multiple tokens in parallel.

baseline: Current two-reader serving configuration with cache disabled or cold prefixes, same model, prompts, decoding, and concurrency.
matched_test: Replay the same two-reader paired workload with prefix cache off and on, alternating order and logging shared-token fraction, time to first token, decode tokens per second, end-to-end p50/p95 latency, KV memory, and cache-hit rate. Include short and long outputs.
decision_rule: Keep caching only if warm-cache end-to-end p50 falls by at least 10% without p95 or answer-quality regression; mark the result inconclusive if shared-prefix hit rate is low. The acceptable KV-memory increase is explicitly unset until measured.
uncertainty: The prefix-caching paper uses larger multi-agent workflows and up to H100 class hardware; speculative decoding results depend on a useful draft model. Neither directly measures two Qwen3-8B readers.

question: For paper QA, whole long paper or iterative selected-passage search/inspection?

sources.title: Drilling Down into the Discourse Structure with LLMs for Long Document Question Answering
Decomposing Retrieval Failures in RAG for Long-Document Financial Question Answering

recommendation: Use iterative search and inspection of selected passages, with explicit evidence coverage checks and a fallback to broader paper inspection on uncertain or multi-hop cases.

claims.text: On QASPER evidence retrieval, the D3 authors report 99.6% of their best zero-shot baseline performance using 26% of its tokens.
The FinanceBench paper identifies missed relevant pages or chunks despite finding the correct long document.

baseline: One pass supplying the whole available paper text to the same reader and answer prompt, within an equalized context budget.
matched_test: On the same 40 questions, compare full-paper input with bounded iterative search/read at equal model and output limits. Independently mark required evidence spans, supported-answer quality, missed-evidence cases, input tokens, latency, and execution errors.
decision_rule: Adopt selected-passage reading if independently reviewed supported-answer passes are no lower than full-paper, missed required evidence increases by at most 1/40, and median input tokens fall by at least 25%. Treat small sample uncertainty explicitly.
uncertainty: The QASPER discourse study tested different models and a structured retriever; selected passages can omit global or multi-hop context. The project question set is a development comparison, not a held-out leaderboard.

question: With capacity to review ~100 more trajectories, prioritize teacher-generated traces or manually corrected failure cases?

sources.title: PROOF-Gen: From Optimized Data to Better Distillation
Speculative Rollback Correction for Quality-Diverse Web Agent Imitation

recommendation: Prioritize manually corrected failure cases from the student reader, especially unsupported answers with successful execution. Retain a smaller teacher-trace sample as a comparator.

claims.text: PROOF-Gen reports that generate-and-filter teacher data discards hard failed scenarios and proposes recovering passing traces from failures.
The SRC study uses bounded teacher review to locate harmful deviations in student agent branches.

baseline: Generate-and-filter teacher traces or the existing 35 verified trajectories without targeted correction.
matched_test: Use the review budget on 50 student failure cases and 50 teacher-generated traces from matched questions. Blind reviewers label executable validity, evidence location, support, and novel corrective action; replay each corrected trace. If later training is authorized, compare equal-size datasets on named held-out questions.
decision_rule: Favor corrected failures for the next dataset only if at least 10 more of 50 reviewed cases provide replay-valid, independently support-checked useful supervision than the matched teacher set. Training threshold is explicitly unset pending a held-out evaluation protocol.
uncertainty: The cited agent studies use web or tool benchmarks and different teachers; manual correction quality and time per case are unmeasured. A near-miss in those studies may differ from a paper-QA support failure.
